questions.question: Part 3 of the Indian Constitution enlists how many groups of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __6.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** The Fundamental Rights​

__
 
• Fundamental Rights are granted to every person in India by the Constitution.
 
• The idea of fundamental rights was borrowed from the constitution of The USA.
 
• Fundamental rights are present in Part III of the constitution from article 12 to article 35.
 
• Part III of the Constitution is described as the* Magna Carta* of India.
 
• ‘Magna Carta’, the Charter of Rights issued by King John of England in 1215 was the first written document relating to the Fundamental Rights of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India has 6 Fundamental rights
 
 
• Right to equality (Art 14 to Art 18)
 
• Right to Freedom {Art 19 to Art 22)
 
• Right against Exploitation (Art 23 and Art 24 )
 
• Right to Freedom of Religion (Art 25 to Art 28)
 
• Cultural and Educational Rights (Art 29 to Art 30)
 
• Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art 32)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Originally the constitution had 7 Fundamental rights.
 
• Right to property (Art 31) which was a fundamental right originally was removed from the fundamental rights by the 44th amendment,1978 and was declared a legal right under art 300-A
 
• The Part III of the constitution is termed as the *Magna Carta* of India.
 
• Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art 32) is considered the heart and soul of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The constitution of India is the longest written constitution in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Fundamental Rights

 
 
• Article 12 – Definition of a state
 
• Article 13 – Right to make law
 
• Article 13A – Judicial Review
 
 
 
• Article (14-18) – Right to Equality
 
 
• Article 14 – Equality before the law.
 
• Article 15 – Prohibition of Discrimination on the basis of religion, race, sex, and place of birth. 
 
• Article 16 – Equality of opportunity in relation to public employment.
 
• Article 17 – Abolish Untouchability.
 
• Article 18 – Elimination of titles.
 
 
 
• Article (19-22) – Right to Freedom
 
 
• Article 19 – Protection of certain rights in relation to the freedom of speech, expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession.
 
• Article 20 – Protection in respect of conviction for offences.
 
• Article 21 – The Safety of Life and Personal Liberty.
 
• Article 21A – Right to Education.
 
• Article 22 – In some cases security against detention.
 
 
 
• Article (23-24) – Rights against exploitation
 
 
• Article 23 – Prevention of Trafficking of humans and forced labour.
 
• Article 24 – Prevention of employment of children in factories, etc.
 
 
 
• Article (25-28) – Right to freedom of religion
 
 
• Article 25 – freedom of condolences and promotion of free professional, practice, and secularism.
 
• Article 26 – Freedom of managing trustworthy matters.
 
• Article 27 – Freedom to pay taxes for the promotion of any particular religion.
 
• Article 28 – Freedom in the form of independent instruction in independent education.
 
 
 
• Articles (29-30) – Culture and Education Rights
 
 
• Article 29 – Protection of Minority Interests
 
• Article 30 – Right to Minorities and to establish and administer the educational Institutions.
 
• Article 31 – The overall acquisition of the property (Now it is not a fundamental right)
 
 
 
• Article (32) – Right to Constitutional Remedies

• He suggested that all matter is made up of tiny, indivisible particles called atoms, which combine in fixed ratios to form compounds.

• Dalton's work on atomic theory was groundbreaking and laid the foundation for modern chemistry.
 
• He was also the first scientist to study the **behavior of gases** and to develop a method for **measuring the relative weights of atoms**.

questions.question: In the early nineteenth century, who demonstrated that there are fourteen space lattices, or regularly repeating arrangements of points in space, that differ in symmetry and geometry?

• The smallest group of symmetrically aligned atoms which can be repeated in an array to make up the entire crystal is called a unit cell.

questions.question: A group of men decided to do a job in 11 days but 16 men left the work after each day. The work, as a result, got completed in 15 days. How many men were there initially in the group?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work planned = 11 × M (where M is initial men).

Actual work done = Sum of men over 15 days = $\frac{15}{2}$ [2M + (15 − 1)(−16)].

11M = 15M − 1680.

4M = 1680 ⇒ M = 420.

**∴ The correct answer is 420 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Planned completion time = 11 days

Actual completion time = 15 days

Number of men leaving daily = 16

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Men × Number of Days

Sum of Arithmetic Progression (Sₙ) = $\frac{n}{2}$ [2a + (n − 1)d]

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency (Avg Men)**
 
 

 Planned Group

 x − 112
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial number of men be x.

⇒ Total work planned = 11 × x = 11x man-days.

⇒ Actual work is the sum of men over 15 days: x + (x − 16) + (x − 32) + ... up to 15 terms.

⇒ Total work done = $\frac{15}{2}$ [2x + (15 − 1) × (−16)]

⇒ 11x = $\frac{15}{2}$ [2x − 224]

⇒ 11x = 15 × (x − 112)

⇒ 11x = 15x − 1680

⇒ 4x = 1680

⇒ x = 420

**∴ The correct answer is 420 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Concept

Work is calculated as the product of the number of workers and the time taken (W = M × D). If the workforce is constant, M₁D₁ = M₂D₂.

Sum of Arithmetic Progression

When the number of workers changes by a constant amount each day, the total work is the sum of an AP: Sₙ = $\frac{n}{2}$[2a + (n − 1)d].

Average Workforce

In a linear decrease/increase of workers, the average number of workers per day is equal to the number of workers on the middle day of the period.</p

⇒ cosec 30° = 1 ÷ sin 30°

Trigonometric functions have reciprocal pairs: cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the active sentence, "The farmers are harvesting the crops.", "the farmers" is the subject, "are harvesting" is the present continuous tense, and "the crops" is the object.
 
• **In passive voice: "The crops" **becomes the subject.
 
• The verb** "are harvesting" **needs to be in the form of "**to be + past participle".** For present continuous, **"are"** stays to indicate the present tense, **"being"** is added as part of the passive construction, and **"harvested"** is the past participle form of **"harvest".**
 
• **"By the farmers"** shows who is performing the action.
 
• Therefore, the sentence "The farmers are harvesting the crops." in passive voice is* "The crops are being harvested by the farmers."*​

Hence, the correct answer is '**option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"The crops are harvested by farmers." **- This is the simple present tense, not the present continuous.
 
• **"The crops have been harvested by the farmers." **- This is the present perfect tense, not the present continuous.
 
• **"The crops are been harvested by the farmers." **- This is grammatically incorrect because "are been" is not a proper verb form.
 
• **"The crops are being harvested by the farmers." **- This **correctly **reflects the present continuous tense in passive voice.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

The professor's lectures are very conventional and so __tedious__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **: Interesting.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tedious: **means something that is too long, slow, or dull; tiresome or monotonous. 
 
• We are looking for a word that means the opposite of dull or boring. 
 
• Interesting: This word means that something is engaging or arousing curiosity or interest. It is the direct opposite of tedious, as it implies that something is far from dull or boring. (रोचक) 
 
 
• **For Example: **The novel's plot was interesting and kept readers engaged.
 
 
 
• The professor’s lectures, described as tedious, would be the opposite of interesting, which would mean they are engaging and hold attention.
 
• Therefore, the correct antonym of "tedious" is "interesting" because it directly contrasts the idea of something being dull or monotonous. 

Hence, the correct answer is **'option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Informative:** While something tedious can also be informative, the word "informative" doesn't serve as an antonym. It simply means providing useful or interesting information, which doesn't convey the opposite of tedium. (सूचनाप्रद)

 
 
• For Example: The workshop was very informative, providing a lot of new information.
 
 
 
• **Idle:** The word "idle" means not active or in use, or without purpose or effect; pointless. This does not directly oppose the concept of being tedious. (निष्क्रिय) 
 
 
• For Example: The machines remained idle during the power outage.
 
 
 
• **Boring:** This is a synonym for tedious, not an antonym. "Boring" means not interesting; tedious. (उबाऊ)
 
 
• For Example: The long lecture was quite boring and many students struggled to stay attentive.

• **Sentence A** gives historical context following the introduction, explaining when Android began and its initial purpose. 
 
• **Sentence B **continues the timeline, detailing the change in direction for the Android project to focus on an operating system for smartphones. 
 
• **Sentence D** then concludes the paragraph with information about a significant event in Android's history, its acquisition by Google, which brought substantial changes to the operating system.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

B. Epics from mythologies like the Mahabharata and Ramayana are likened to classic Greek works like the Odyssey and Iliad and between 1 and 1000 AD, India was lauded as the ‘Golden Bird’ for its GDP, which was higher than China at the time.

C. Luminaries like Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore, as well as the arts of literature, music, dance, the software industry, Ayurveda, etc., generate a staggering array of soft power assets that highlight India's appeal to the world's population. 

D. With Ashoka, Buddha, and Gandhi serving as the primary leaders, Indians are known for their core values of respect, harmony, and fraternity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph begins by introducing the central vision of India and sets an optimistic tone about its democratic and non-threatening global leadership.
 
• **Sentence A is the first sentence** as it sets the vision and current perspective:
 
 
• "India has an upbeat vision of a liberal, nonviolent, relatively pluralistic democracy with non-threatening global leadership."
 
 
 
• **Sentence C follows** as it highlights modern soft power assets, reflecting how this vision translates into contemporary influence:
 
 
• "Luminaries like Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore, as well as the arts of literature, music, dance, the software industry, Ayurveda, etc., generate a staggering array of soft power assets that highlight India's appeal to the world's population."
 
 
 
• **Sentence D is the third sentence** because it connects these modern influences with historical figures and the values they promoted:
 
 
• "With Ashoka, Buddha, and Gandhi serving as the primary leaders, Indians are known for their core values of respect, harmony, and fraternity."
 
 
 
• **Sentence B is the fourth** as it delves into the deep historical context, providing a foundation for the modern vision and influence:
 
 
• "Epics from mythologies like the Mahabharata and Ramayana are likened to classic Greek works like the Odyssey and Iliad and between 1 and 1000 AD, India was lauded as the ‘Golden Bird’ for its GDP, which was higher than China at the time."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **ACDB**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"India has an upbeat vision of a liberal, nonviolent, relatively pluralistic democracy with non-threatening global leadership. Luminaries like Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore, as well as the arts of literature, music, dance, the software industry, Ayurveda, etc., generate a staggering array of soft power assets that highlight India's appeal to the world's population. With Ashoka, Buddha, and Gandhi serving as the primary leaders, Indians are known for their core values of respect, harmony, and fraternity. Epics from mythologies like the Mahabharata and Ramayana are likened to classic Greek works like the Odyssey and Iliad and between 1 and 1000 AD, India was lauded as the ‘Golden Bird’ for its GDP, which was higher than China at the time."
